civics_questions.question_text: What is the supreme law of the land?
What does the Constitution do?
civics_questions.official_answer: It sets up the government. It defines the government's powers. It protects the basic rights of Americans.

civics_questions.question_text: The first three words of the Constitution are very important. What are these words?
What is an amendment?
civics_questions.official_answer: A change (to the Constitution). An addition (to the Constitution).

civics_questions.question_text: What do we call the first ten amendments to the Constitution?
What is one right or freedom from the First Amendment?
civics_questions.official_answer: Speech, Religion, Assembly, Press, or Petition the government

civics_questions.question_text: How many amendments does the Constitution have?
What did the Declaration of Independence do?
civics_questions.official_answer: Announced our independence (from Great Britain). Declared our independence (from Great Britain). Said that the United States is free (from Great Britain).

civics_questions.question_text: What year was the Declaration of Independence adopted?
There are four amendments to the Constitution about who can vote. Describe one of them.
civics_questions.official_answer: Citizens 18 or older can vote. You don't have to pay to vote. Any citizen can vote (not just men). A male citizen of any race can vote.

civics_questions.question_text: What is the name of the President of the United States now?
What is the name of the Vice President of the United States now?
If the President can no longer serve, who becomes President?
If both the President and the Vice President can no longer serve, who becomes President?
Who is the Speaker of the House of Representatives now?
Who makes federal laws?
civics_questions.official_answer: Congress. Senate and House of Representatives. The legislative branch.

civics_questions.question_text: What are the two parts of the U.S. Congress?
civics_questions.official_answer: The Senate and the House of Representatives

civics_questions.question_text: How many U.S. Senators are there?
How many years do we elect each U.S. Senator?
Who is one of your state's U.S. Senators now?
How many voting members does the House of Representatives have?
We elect a U.S. Representative for how many years?
Who is your U.S. Representative?
What are the two major political parties in the United States?
What is the political party of the President now?
What is the executive branch of our government?
civics_questions.official_answer: The President, Cabinet, and agencies under the Cabinet members. The President enforces the laws of our country.

civics_questions.question_text: What is the legislative branch of our government?
civics_questions.official_answer: Congress. Senate and House of Representatives. Congress makes federal laws.

civics_questions.question_text: What is the judicial branch of our government?
civics_questions.official_answer: The Supreme Court. Courts. The judicial branch interprets laws.

civics_questions.question_text: What are the three branches of government?
How many justices are on the Supreme Court?
Who is the Chief Justice of the United States?
Can the President serve more than two terms?
How long is a term for the President?
What does the President's Cabinet do?
What is the most important right granted to U.S. citizens?
civics_questions.official_answer: The right to vote. Freedom of speech. Freedom of religion. The right to petition the government.

civics_questions.question_text: What is naturalization?
civics_questions.official_answer: The process to become a U.S. citizen

civics_questions.question_text: What is the most important right we want for all our people?
civics_questions.official_answer: Freedom. Liberty. Freedom of speech. The ability to pursue happiness.

civics_questions.question_text: How many full terms is a President elected for?
Name one right guaranteed by the Bill of Rights.
civics_questions.official_answer: Freedom of speech, religion, assembly, petition, or press. The right to bear arms. Protection against unreasonable search and seizure. The right to a speedy trial. The right to remain silent. The right to an attorney.

civics_questions.question_text: What is the first amendment?
civics_questions.official_answer: Freedom of speech, religion, assembly, petition, and press

civics_questions.question_text: What is the Second Amendment?
civics_questions.official_answer: The right to bear arms. The right to own a gun.

notes: This is a representative sample of USCIS civics questions. The complete 100-question (pre-Oct 2025) and 128-question (Oct 2025+) sets should be sourced from official USCIS materials. Questions marked with [PLACEHOLDER] require dynamic content replacement at runtime.
